result.description: metais reads, validates and renders METAIS packages, and helps author them.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Print what a supplier reads first: the package's identity, its guide, its inputs, outputs, references and examples, and the commands to run next.
commands.detail:
The package is a packed package file or a source directory. Before it prints anything, inspect verifies the whole package: every entry's name and data, the digest of every entry and of the package, the manifest under the specification version it declares, every schema, and each compiled file against the sources it is derived from. A package that fails any check is refused with every finding of the check, and nothing of it is printed.

The digest of a source directory is the digest of the package metais pack would write from it, computed in memory; nothing is written.

A guide of more than 60 lines or 6144 bytes is cut to its first 40 lines, within 4096 bytes; --guide prints it whole, and nothing else.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

flags.name: --guide
flags.description: Print only the package's identity and its whole guide.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: The package's summary: its title, name and version, description, specification version, form and digest, then the sections Guide, Inputs, Outputs, References, Assets, Examples and Read next; with --guide, the guide's Markdown alone.

refusals.cause: A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.

next.why: Lists every limit with its default; a limit can be lowered and never raised.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Write a new package's source directory, with an input, a template and an example.
commands.detail:
Writes eight files into <dir>: metais.yaml, one input with its schema and meaning document, one template, one example with its inputs and expected output, and a .gitattributes that keeps git from converting line endings. The scaffold is a small package to edit rather than an empty one.

The package's name is --name, or else the last element of <dir> as written. When <dir> is omitted or ends in . or .., --name is required: metais never looks up the working directory's name. The name must satisfy the package name rule.

<dir> is created, with its missing parents, when it does not exist. An existing <dir> must be empty, apart from names beginning with . (such as .git) other than .compiled and .gitattributes, and files ending .metais; init never overwrites, and refuses anything else, listing up to ten of the entries it found. A failed write stops init, which lists the files it wrote and removes none of them.

operands.description: The directory to write into, created when absent; the current directory when omitted.

flags.name: --name
flags.description: The package's name. It is required when <dir> is omitted or its last element is . or ..; otherwise it defaults to that element.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.description: Report the files init would write, and write nothing.

flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Check a package without data, and report every finding of every step at once.
commands.detail:
The package is a source directory, the current directory when omitted, or a packed package file. check reads nothing but the package and writes nothing. It runs every step in order: the source tree, the entries, the limits of the package pack would write, the manifest and its guide's links, every schema with its defaults, examples, consts, enums and required names, every template, the cross-reference of templates against schemas, Office Open XML text runs, the examples' layout, and the compiled form. Each step runs whatever an earlier one found; a step whose input could not be made is named in one report.step_skipped finding.

A package that cannot be read at all — its container, its entry names, its digests or its source tree — is refused with the findings every command gives it.

check exits 1 when any finding is an error; warnings do not fail it.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A source directory, or a packed package file; the current directory when omitted. - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: Every finding, then a line counting the errors, warnings and notes, then the Next: block.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the tool's version and the specification versions it implements.
commands.detail:
The tool's version is a semantic version. Its version is independent of the specification's: a release may implement a new minor version of the specification without a new major version of the tool. Every specification version the tool implements is listed, ascending, so a caller tests membership without knowing which minor versions imply which.

metais --version, before any command, is this command.

commands.name: limits
commands.description: List every resource limit, with its default, unit and class.
commands.detail:
Every size, count and ratio metais reads, computes or writes is bounded, and every bound has a name and a default. A package within every package limit is portable: every conforming tool accepts it at the defaults. A limit may be lowered for one run, and is never raised.

A default in bytes is shown in the largest of KiB, MiB and GiB (powers of 1024) that it is a whole number of; --json gives every default as a number in the limit's unit.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Print the overview, a command's help, or a topic.
commands.detail:
With no operand, prints the overview: the commands by group, the global flags, the topics and the exit codes. With a command's name, prints that command's help, as metais <command> --help does. With a topic, prints the topic.

topics.name: inputs
topics.title: Supplying a package's inputs, and which source wins.
topics.text:
A package declares its inputs, each with a schema, and a caller supplies them
from three sources, applied in this order, each to the result of the one before:

1. The data directory, given with --data: one file per input, named after the
   input with the extension of its form (vendor.json, criteria.csv), or one
   directory per collection input. Each gives its input's whole value. A file
   that names no declared input is a finding, and so is a second file for one
   input.
2. Each --inputs-json, in command-line order: a JSON object whose members are
   input names, each replacing that input's whole value; values are never
   merged. --inputs-json - reads the object from standard input, once.
3. Each path set, in command-line order: --set /input/pointer=text sets one
   value at a JSON Pointer whose first token is an input's name, coercing the
   text by the schema; --set-json /input/pointer=json sets it to a JSON value,
   which is how null, an array or an object is set. Each replaces only the value
   at its pointer.

The order is fixed by kind, not by position: every --inputs-json applies before
every path set, wherever they are written, and among one kind the later wins. To
change one nested value and keep the rest, use a path set; --inputs-json
replaces the whole input.

Defaults from the schemas are applied after all three, and then the inputs are
validated, every finding at once.

topics.name: globs
topics.title: The patterns that select a package's entries.
topics.text:
A glob selects a package's entries by path. It is matched against the whole
entry path, segment by segment, with / as the separator, and is case-sensitive.

  *       matches any run of characters within one segment.
  ?       matches one character other than /.
  [...]   matches one character in a class; lo-hi is a range.
  [^...]  matches one character not in a class.
  \       makes the next character literal.
  **      standing alone as a segment, matches zero or more whole segments; **
          anywhere else is a usage error.

There are no braces. *, ?, [...] and ** never match a segment that begins with a
dot; a pattern segment that itself begins with a dot matches one. So **/*.md
does not reach into .compiled/, and .compiled/** does. A pattern with no
wildcard that names a directory selects every entry beneath it.

topics.name: json
topics.title: The JSON document every command prints with --json.
topics.text:
With --json, a run prints exactly one JSON document on standard output: compact
UTF-8 with no byte order mark, one line ending in one LF, HTML escaping off, and
standard error empty. Its members are always present, in this order:

  format    The document's name and major version, metais.<command>/<major>.
  ok        True when the command completed and no finding is an error.
  findings  The findings, in the specification's order; [] when there are none.
            A usage error is a finding too.
  summary   The exact counts of errors, warnings and info, how many findings are
            listed and omitted, and the count of each code.
  result    The command's result, or null when it was refused before producing
            one.
  next      The commands to run next, each {"run", "why"}; [] when there is
            nothing to suggest, and never empty after a refusal.

The exit status is the same with and without --json, and --json is honoured even
on a command line that does not parse. Within a major version a format only
gains members and enumeration values: ignore a member you do not know, and read
an unknown value as other.

The formats:
  metais.inspect/1  metais inspect
  metais.init/1     metais init
  metais.check/1    metais check
  metais.version/1  metais version
  metais.limits/1   metais limits
  metais.help/1     metais help
  metais.usage/1    a line that names no command

topics.name: exit-codes
topics.title: What each exit status means.
topics.text:
metais exits with the same status with and without --json:

  0  Success, warnings included; help, version and limits.
  1  An error in content: invalid inputs, a failing check or test, an output
     refused by its schema or its path, a package's own defect under an
     authoring command, or a warning under --fail-on warning.
  2  A defect in metais itself (internal.error), or the Go runtime's status
     after a crash.
  3  The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, a missing or extra
     operand, a malformed or repeated flag, or no command at all.
  4  The package is refused: not found, unreadable, out of specification, a
     digest mismatch, an unsupported specification version or a package limit;
     or a package's own defect under a consuming command.
  5  The destination is refused: not empty without --overwrite, a link or
     special file in the way, or a failed write.

When several apply, the first in the order 2, 3, 4, 1, 5 is the status: fixing a
destination alone would not help a run whose inputs are invalid.

exit_codes.meaning: Success, warnings included; help, version and limits.
An error in content: invalid inputs, a failing check or test, an output refused by its schema or its path, a package's own defect under an authoring command, or a warning under --fail-on warning.
A defect in metais itself (internal.error), or the Go runtime's status after a crash.
The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, a missing or extra operand, a malformed or repeated flag, or no command at all.
The package is refused: not found, unreadable, out of specification, a digest mismatch, an unsupported specification version or a package limit; or a package's own defect under a consuming command.
The destination is refused: not empty without --overwrite, a link or special file in the way, or a failed write.
